key_insight: A trapped non-wetting droplet in a capillary tube can be unpinned by non-resonant acoustic streaming combined with a static pressure gradient, with an optimal attenuation condition that minimizes required drive.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design rule for lower-power acoustic mobilization of trapped fluids in porous media, with direct implications for enhanced oil recovery and downhole microfluidic control.
method: Expanded the hydrodynamic equations to second order to capture bulk acoustic-wind forcing.
Derived a critical acoustic amplitude needed to overcome capillary pinning.
Included wall-boundary and thermo-viscous dissipation effects to obtain an optimum condition and transport-velocity expression.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivation plus numerical validation and comparison against legacy industrial frequency baselines.
watch_item: The theory depends on idealized capillary geometry and attenuation matching, so performance may shift in heterogeneous formations or when material properties are poorly known.
paper_title: Unpinning of trapped oil droplets via non-resonant acoustic streaming in capillary tubes
